summary.headline: Shankara Buildpro Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore; steel volume grew 10% to 2.5 lakh tons and EBITDA margin was 3.26%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore and PAT rose 12% YoY to Rs 35.8 crore, led by steel volume growth and a recovery in non-steel. Management said April-May were weak due to West Asia-linked energy inflation and steel price volatility, with conditions improving through June and July. EBITDA was Rs 62 crore (3.26% margin), which management said included about Rs 10 crore of inventory erosion (roughly 50 bps) from a price correction in May-June. Management reiterated the 1.2 million-ton steel volume target, 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth, and a 3.5% steady-state EBITDA margin, and proposed a 1:5 stock split.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 35.8 crore (also cited as Rs 35.9 crore)

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Volume of 2.5 lakh tons (+10% YoY) and revenue of Rs 1,725 crore (+21% YoY); pipes, tubes, flats and roofing all grew in volume. Management said the 1.2 million-ton FY27 target is intact.

segments.name: Non-steel
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 165 crore (+15% YoY). Fittings and sanitary ware, the largest category, grew 32%; accessories and electricals grew about 40% on a smaller base; tiles were hit hardest in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume target of 1.2 million tons, with 20% steel volume growth and 25% non-steel growth reiterated.
Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 3.5%+; management said about 3.8% would have been reached without the Rs 10 crore inventory erosion.
Medium term (FY28 onward): EBITDA margin of around 4%, while maintaining 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.
Target of 2 million tons in around 4 years; the 20% growth path is the baseline, with new territories and stores as upside.
About 5 more fulfilment centres or stores planned in the coming quarters, taking FY27 additions to roughly 8-9 (3 added in Q1).
Proposed 1:5 stock split (face value Rs 10 to Rs 2), pending shareholder and regulatory approvals; total paid-up capital unchanged.
capex_capacity: Three fulfilment centres/stores added in Q1 FY27 (Mangalore, Mumbai, Thrissur), plus 34 customer touchpoints across 45 towns and cities in 10 states.
About 5 more fulfilment centres planned in the coming quarters.
Planned investment in value-added steel infrastructure (cut-to-length, laser cutting) and warehousing.
Cash use priorities: private-label products (with promotion spend), value-added steel investment, and reducing acceptance-based borrowing. Acquisitions are 'on the table' but none named.
demand_pricing: Steel prices spiked in March-April, then corrected sharply in May-June, causing inventory erosion of about Rs 10 crore; prices have stabilised over July and early August.
Management said the Q4 FY26 inventory gain was about Rs 15 crore.
Volume recovered in June (about 1 lakh MT of rebound cited) and management said the momentum continued into July.
Non-steel tile demand was near zero in April (Morbi gas/energy shock) and recovered in May-June; PVC/UPVC roofing uptake is good.
Competitive intensity from well-funded enterprise-focused players has eased in the last couple of quarters; management is de-prioritising TMT and focusing on flats.
Retail accounts for about 50-55% of total volume. Ticket sizes range from Rs 500 to Rs 1.5 crore across 25 verticals, 75 categories and over 100 brands, with over 2 lakh SKUs.

qa_highlights.question: Can 22-23% volume growth be achieved for the rest of FY27 to reach 1.2 MT, given the high H2 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said June volume growth was very positive and July continued the trend, and he is confident of 1.2 MT barring unforeseen headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What were the margin impacts from fixed-price contracts and inventory, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carried over from March into April forced supply at high prices, and the May-June price drop eroded about Rs 10 crore (about 50 bps). Ex this, margin would have been about 3.8%; steady state 3.5%+ is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for 25% non-steel growth when peers are not showing similar optimism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 32% growth in CP and sanitary ware, a tile recovery from May-June, and PVC/UPVC roofing traction; the CP/sanitary segment is expected to drive most of the growth.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the interest cost, given about Rs 75 crore of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Alex Varghese said about Rs 500 crore of acceptances (LCs opened and discounted, with the company bearing interest) bring total borrowings to about Rs 575 crore; the interest cost mainly comes from acceptances.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% revenue growth achievable at a 3.5% EBITDA margin, and is there margin expansion in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhananjay Mirlay Srinivas said the company is on track for 20% volume growth at 3.5% margin, and medium-term aims for about 4% EBITDA margin with 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: How long to reach 2 MT, and what new categories are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 4 years to 2 MT via new territories, stores and market share gains; new steel infrastructure for cut-to-length and value-added products, and expanding white-label private labels in retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume/price split of the 21% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said price played little part; steel prices were high and then softened, so the effect was largely neutral. He said a detailed split would be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for a 3.5% margin when adjusted Q1 margin is about 3.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said management is taking a cautious path because steel inventory gains and losses are outside its control, and it prefers to be prudent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel business profitability and outlook for flats?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-steel has an 8-10% EBITDA margin, so steel is trending above 3% overall; diversifying into flats and multiple steel products should help grow EBITDA.

risks_watch: Whether June-July volume momentum (management cited ~1 lakh MT rebound in June) holds, given 1.2 MT FY27 target needs roughly 22-24% volume growth over Q2-Q4 against a high second-half base.
Steel price volatility: any inventory gain or loss outside 3.5% steady-state margin; management hopes prices stay stable in Q2 but gave no quantified inventory outlook.
Non-steel 25% growth target versus Q1 at 15%; depends on tiles recovering after Morbi energy shock and CP/sanitary sustaining ~32% growth.

Finance cost and borrowing: ~Rs 500 crore of acceptances (LCs opened and discounted, interest borne by company) within ~Rs 575 crore total borrowings; watch whether acceptances are reduced as management indicated.

Competitive intensity from well-funded enterprise players has eased, but management said it is not fully off; company is de-prioritising TMT and focusing on flats. Watch whether enterprise-segment margins improve.
Pending approvals for the proposed 1:5 stock split (face value Rs 10 to Rs 2) and timing of the ~5 additional fulfilment centres/stores planned.

summary.management_tone: Confident on volume recovery and the 1.2 MT target, with management citing June and July momentum and stabilising prices. Cautious on margins: management kept the 3.5% steady-state target below the ~3.8% adjusted Q1 margin, citing inventory moves outside its control, and gave no volume/price split (said it would share offline).
